messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about Employment and Higher and further education in Bavaria during the 1970s, matching this research need: Data on Munich university and technical college graduates covering school background, study trajectories, social origins, career entry, job conditions, employer expectations, income, career prospects, and life/job satisfaction.
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

queries: Munich university Fachhochschule graduates 1970s survey social origin career income job satisfaction dataset
Münchner Hochschulabsolventen 1970er Berufsstart soziale Herkunft Arbeitszufriedenheit Datensatz
GESIS Absolventen Münchner Hochschulen 1970 Beruf Erwartungen Arbeitgeber Einkommen

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"Hochschulausbildung und Beruf (College Education and Profession) — GESIS Dataset, ZA1458","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.1458","justification":"Excellent match for the research need. This historical dataset examines graduates of the University of Munich and the Technical University of Munich who completed their studies in 1972. The survey was conducted in May–June 1975, making it directly relevant to employment and higher education in Bavaria during the 1970s. It provides individual-level information on university graduates and their transition from higher education into professional life. Its subject matter aligns closely with the requested investigation of educational backgrounds, study experiences, social origins, employment outcomes, and professional careers. The dataset was produced by Walter Hornstein and Georg Kärtner, with the German Youth Institute in Munich (Deutsches Jugendinstitut) identified as a contributing institution. It is archived by GESIS and classified under employment, higher education, and university research. This is the strongest identified dataset because its geographical coverage, graduate population, and historical period match the research requirements precisely. Access is restricted to academic research and teaching and requires written authorization from the data depositor. The detailed variable documentation should be consulted to confirm coverage of employer expectations, income, career prospects, and life and job satisfaction."},{"title":"Absolventenpanel 1979 (Graduate Panel 1979) — GESIS Dataset, ZA5185","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/research_data/ZA5185?lang=de","justification":"Relevant complementary dataset examining university graduates' educational experiences, professional orientations, and transitions into employment. Data collection took place between 1979 and 1984. The survey covers attitudes toward university education, academic careers, professional work, gender roles, social inequality, personal values, and expectations concerning employment. Participants were drawn from several academic disciplines, including medicine, economics, natural sciences, engineering, and modern languages. It is particularly useful for studying graduates' professional aspirations, perceptions of employment, and the relationship between university education and occupational expectations. However, its geographical coverage is not confirmed as specific to Munich or Bavaria, and part of the collection period extends into the 1980s. It is therefore a secondary match rather than a direct substitute for the Munich graduate dataset."},{"title":"Abiturienten-Follow-up 1976/77 (Abiturientenpanel) — Graduate Panel","url_or_doi":"https://b2find.eudat.eu/dataset/6e13f967-ae47-5f66-9fac-103fe5c3b79d","justification":"Historical longitudinal education dataset relevant to the transition from secondary schooling into university studies and professional life during the 1970s. It includes information on educational expectations, university admission, perceptions of academic requirements, intended fields of study, professional goals, anticipated earnings, social status, and expectations concerning graduates' labor-market opportunities. The dataset is valuable for analyzing school backgrounds, educational aspirations, academic trajectories, and early career expectations. It can provide contextual evidence for understanding the educational pathways of the generation entering higher education during the 1970s. However, it is not specifically restricted to Munich university graduates or Bavarian institutions, and its coverage of actual employment conditions, earnings, and job satisfaction is less directly established than that of a graduate employment survey."}]}
